_provenance.adjudicator_detail: Claude Opus 5.5 subagent (S2 adjudication pass). No parser output was viewed and no text was extracted from any PDF.
_provenance.annotator_detail: annotator-1's file records a Claude Opus 5.5 subagent; annotator-2's file records only its label. Both came from the same workflow run. Treat them as two runs of one model, not two independent humans. annotator-1 also read the seed gold.json (agent C's YOLO/DDPM anchors) before annotating, so its YOLO and DDPM are not blind to the seed.
_provenance.method: Both annotators wrote gold from page images at 130 dpi (pdftoppm), with 220-300 dpi crops where a reading was ambiguous, and no text extraction. The adjudicator aligned their units with iaa.py and re-rendered every page at 130 dpi. Each disagreement was decided from the image, using 200-300 dpi crops and, for DDPM p2, a row ink profile of a 300 dpi grey render (image analysis only). The merge is mechanical (adjudicate.py), with every ruling listed there.
_provenance.pdf_operations: curl download of the versioned arXiv URL; shasum -a 256; pdfinfo (page count only); pdftoppm rendering. Nothing else.

iaa.caveat: The two annotators share a model and annotator-1 saw the seed, so this agreement is an upper bound on what independent humans would reach, not a ceiling for parser scores. The adjudicator overrode BOTH annotators on two DDPM units where they agreed, so agreement is not correctness.

owner_rulings_needed: cont after a display equation. Three units: YOLO 'which gives us', DDPM 'What distinguishes', DDPM 'The forward process variances'. Each carries alt_kind 'body' for the case where cont is restricted to column and page breaks.
Front-unit granularity: one unit per role group (names / affiliations / contacts / date), or per stacked author column. Two units depend on this: FlashAttention affiliations and the SBERT URL.
Small caps are written in typographic case. The scorer must compare case-insensitively whichever way this is ruled.
conventions: order holds running content only: front, heading, body (one unit per printed paragraph), cont. Captions go in floats, display equations in equations, and running heads, page numbers, the arXiv stamp, venue footers, footnotes and figure-internal text in furniture.

front: the title is one unit, however many lines it has. A centred block gives one unit per role group: names line(s), affiliation line(s), contact line(s) (URL / e-mail), date. Stacked per-author columns (name / affiliation / e-mail) give one unit per column, anchored by the name.
body: a printed paragraph, cut where an indent (indented styles) or a paragraph skip (unindented styles) says one starts.
cont: the same paragraph resuming after a column break or a page break (including one that a float sits in), or after a display equation (pending owner ruling, alt_kind 'body').

anchor: the words both annotators wrote (the shared prefix), as printed. Line-break hyphens are removed and real hyphens kept; ligatures are plain letters; footnote and affiliation markers are dropped, so front anchors stop before the first marker; citation brackets are kept; inline math is flattened (βt, S × S); apostrophes are printed curly. A word split across a column break is anchored as printed in the new column (SBERT 'tic').

Small caps are written in typographic case: a full-size capital in upper case, a small capital in lower case ('FlashAttention', 'Pascal', 'Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization'). Compare case-insensitively.
Caption anchors include the printed label ('Figure 1:', 'Figure 1.', 'Algorithm 1:'). Strip ^(Figure|Table|Algorithm)\s*\d+[:.] to get the seed's label-free form.
headings: every section and subsection heading on pp1-2 as printed, with its numbering. Bold paragraph lead-ins go under run_in_headings; their paragraph is one body unit.

A unit is [page, kind, anchor] or [page, kind, anchor, {extras}]. Readers expecting three fields should use u[:3]. extras.disputed = true marks a unit where the adjudicator overrode at least one annotator on the unit's existence, extent, kind or anchor words. Case-only harmonisation is listed per paper under adjudication.case_harmonised_anchors instead.
